skill.name: web-accessibility
skill.description: Guides web accessibility implementation using WCAG 2.1, semantic HTML, ARIA, keyboard navigation, screen reader support, and accessibility testing.
skill.summary: Build accessible web interfaces with WCAG 2.1, ARIA, keyboard navigation, and practical testing guidance.
skill.author: supercent-io

security_audit.summary: All 74 static findings were reviewed against SKILL.md and SKILL.toon. The alerts are false positives from Markdown code fences, inline accessibility examples, documentation links, and relative documentation references. No prompt injection, malicious intent, executable shell commands, credential handling, or runtime network or filesystem behavior was found.

static_findings.snippet: - Exclude from focus order → `tabindex="-1"` (programmatic focus only)
- Do not change focus order → avoid using `tabindex="1+"`
- `aria-labelledby`: Reference another element as a label
2. **Alternative Text**: All images must have an `alt` attribute
1. **Do Not Remove Outline**: Never use `outline: none`
- Do not change focus order → avoid using `tabindex="1+"`
2. **Do Not Use tabindex > 0**: Avoid changing focus order
- "Invalid input" ❌ → "Email must be in format: example@domain.com" ✅

content.value_statement: Inaccessible interfaces exclude users and create compliance risk. This skill guides accessible HTML, ARIA, keyboard behavior, visual contrast, and testing.
actual_capabilities: Guides semantic HTML and landmark structure for accessible pages.
Provides keyboard navigation patterns for dropdowns, modals, forms, and tabs.
Explains ARIA labels, live regions, dialog roles, and hidden decorative content.
Applies WCAG contrast rules and visible focus guidance.
Describes automated and manual testing with axe, Lighthouse, keyboard checks, and screen readers.
Includes React and TypeScript examples for common accessible components.
limitations: Does not run accessibility scans or inspect live pages by itself.
Targets WCAG 2.1 guidance; newer standards may need extra checks.
Examples need adaptation to each framework, design system, and product flow.
Does not replace legal review or testing with users with disabilities.

use_cases.title: Build Accessible Components
use_cases.description: Create buttons, forms, modals, dropdowns, and tabs with semantic markup and keyboard support.

use_cases.title: Audit Product Screens
use_cases.description: Review existing pages for labels, focus order, contrast, ARIA usage, and screen reader behavior.

use_cases.title: Prepare WCAG Remediation
use_cases.description: Convert accessibility gaps into practical fixes and acceptance criteria for development teams.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Component
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner audit of a single UI component.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this component for WCAG AA accessibility issues. Focus on semantic HTML, labels, keyboard use, focus states, and screen reader behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Fix Keyboard Behavior
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate repair for menus, dialogs, or tabs.
prompt_templates.prompt: Improve this menu or dialog so it works with Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Space, arrow keys, and Escape. Explain each change.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Accessible Form
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate implementation planning for form workflows.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an accessible form for [purpose] in [framework]. Include labels, errors, required fields, live announcements, and validation guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Test Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a WCAG 2.1 AA test plan for [feature]. Include automated checks, manual keyboard tests, screen reader checks, and acceptance criteria.

output_examples.input: Review a checkout form for accessibility gaps.
output_examples.output: A prioritized checklist covering labels, error messages, focus order, contrast, keyboard behavior, and validation announcements.

output_examples.input: Make a modal usable for keyboard and screen reader users.
output_examples.output: A remediation plan for dialog roles, focus placement, focus trapping, Escape handling, labeling, and return focus behavior.

output_examples.input: Prepare accessibility acceptance criteria for a tab interface.
output_examples.output: Clear criteria for tab roles, arrow key navigation, selected state, panel labeling, and manual test steps.

best_practices: Start with semantic HTML before adding ARIA.
Test every workflow with keyboard only and visible focus.
Pair automated scans with manual screen reader and interaction checks.
anti_patterns: Replacing visible labels with placeholder text only.
Removing focus outlines without providing a clear custom focus style.
Using positive tabindex values to force a custom focus order.

faq.question: What accessibility standard does this skill target?
faq.answer: It focuses on WCAG 2.1 guidance, with a practical default of AA-level implementation.

faq.question: Can it help with ARIA decisions?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains labels, live regions, dialog roles, hidden decorative elements, and when semantic HTML is better.

faq.question: Does it generate complete production components?
faq.answer: It provides implementation patterns and examples, but teams should adapt them to project code and test thoroughly.

faq.question: Does it cover keyboard accessibility?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers Tab order, activation keys, arrow key navigation, Escape handling, and focus management.

faq.question: Can it replace automated accessibility tools?
faq.answer: No. It recommends tools such as axe and Lighthouse, but it does not run scans by itself.

faq.question: Is legal compliance guaranteed?
faq.answer: No. The skill provides technical guidance, but legal compliance depends on jurisdiction, product scope, and expert review.
